articles.title: Andrew Garfield’s The Uprising Sends Mixed Signals on Robin Hood Connection
articles.summary: Focus Features’ The Uprising stars Andrew Garfield in a 1381 Peasants' Revolt drama—but new marketing suggests it might actually be a stealth Robin Hood origin story. “To the rich, he was an outlaw. To the people, he was a hero.
body: This ad revealed the film’s new title as The Uprising: The Rise of Robin Hood. It shows Garfield’s character, dressed in a green hood, emerging from the woods to confront the King and his soldiers. He is accompanied by his fellow highwaymen, who wield bows and arrows. “There will be no peace until we are free. Time to pay,” Garfield’s character declares at swordpoint.
A day after this ad was released the film’s title was changed back to being just The Uprising.

The film’s UK distributor even released a statement denying The Uprising is a Robin Hood movie (via Metro ): “Marketing materials posted by other countries that may appear in the UK online and on social media referencing Robin Hood are not issued or approved by us.”

The Uprising had been understood to be about the Peasants’ Revolt of 1381, which was led by historical figures Wat Tyler (played by Shogun’s Cosmo Jarvis) and John Ball (played by Jamie Bell). Garfield’s character Ploughman was thought to represent the Everyman peasant pushed by misfortune into taking up arms against the crown.
points: Focus Features’ The Uprising stars Andrew Garfield in a 1381 Peasants' Revolt drama—but new marketing suggests it might actually be a stealth Robin Hood origin story.

articles.title: It’s A Good Week If You Like Games That Let You Play As An Animal
articles.summary: After Gamescom Opening Night Live and the Future Games Show, we can't help noticing that there are multiple titles coming up that let players either assume control of an animal or play anthropomorphic characters who resemble human/animal hybrids.
body: Amphibian is a retro RPG that casts players as humanoid frogs on a quest to save their world. As seen in the trailer below, the game apparently commits to its froggy bit by recording all of the dialogue as ribbit sounds. However, the English translations appear on-screen.

Bye Bye Bonnie is also a four-player co-op adventure at a decidedly smaller scale. These creatures are minuscule compared to the world around them. Even their ship is small, although it's large enough that the characters have to jump up and down on the controls to guide it through the obstacles ahead.

Haunted Paws is a "cozy co-op horror" adventure that puts players in control of two puppies that have to rescue their owner from a haunted mansion. These dogs are more conventional than Amphibian's frogs, but they still find ways to drive cars and play video games while staying one paw ahead of some malicious ghosts.

Conversely, Gravhounds leans even harder into anthropomorphic canine heroes with very human-like dogs who have been sent across the galaxy to colonize a planet. It's unclear how these dogs were bred into humanoid beings, but they share a desire to earn a trip back home.

articles.title: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma Opens Up on Future of Physical Games for Next Generation Console Project Helix
articles.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma was cagey when asked if the company’s next console, codenamed Project Helix, will have a disc drive or not, but gave some optimistic insights into its approach to physical games.
body: Speaking with the BBC in August 2026, Sharma didn’t give a straight answer; instead, she said Xbox is currently focused on making its next generation hardware cost-effective and efficient.
“This next generation, we have to be thinking about efficiency and affordability alongside performance," she told the outlet.

"All of the industry needs to start to innovate on affordability and efficiency," she continued. "That is something that we have not had to do. But with the crisis that's currently happening in hardware and components, it is absolutely something all of us need to be thinking about and innovating on and giving people more choice in terms of how they play their console and how they purchase their console."

While she couldn’t outright confirm or deny the existence of a disc drive for Project Helix, Sharma is well-aware of the current debate surrounding physical media, and assured the BBC that she wants to give players a choice when it comes to how they choose to purchase content.

articles.title: Double Fine Productions Makes Brutal Legend Free for 666 Minutes to Honor Tim Curry
articles.summary: Double Fine Productions, who recently regained the rights to its entire catalog following its pivot back to independence after Microsoft parted ways with several studios during its " Xbox reset," is honoring Tim Curry by making Brutal Legend free to download and own on PC for 666 minutes – until…
body: Curry, who passed away today at the age of 80, voiced Doviculus in Double Fine founder Tim Schafer's 2009 heavy metal strategy game Brutal Legend. "Rest in peace, dark prince," the company wrote on its itch.io page where you can download the game on PC. IGN's own Daemon Hatfield loved Brutal Legend, giving it a 9 out of 10 in his review. "Brutal Legend is a tour de force that wraps up humor, music, and clever gameplay into one highly polished package," Daemon wrote. "You haven't played a game quite like this before and won't want to miss it."

Curry was perhaps best known for his role in the cult classic film The Rocky Horror Picture Show, but also appeared in many video games besides Brutal Legend, including Command & Conquer: Red Alert 3 (back in the FMV cutscene days!), Gabriel Knight: Sins of the Fathers, and Dragon Age: Origins.
Double Fine, meanwhile, has announced that it is using its newfound independence to bring back its Amnesia Fortnight game jam as it looks to create its next project(s).

articles.title: Tom Cruise's Unforgettable 10/10 Action Movie is Officially Free to Watch on YouTube
articles.summary: Sometimes, an unexpected cameo can elevate an otherwise solid movie into a genuine cult favorite. Matt Damon’s unhinged performance of “Scotty Doesn’t Know” is the most prominent thing I remember about 2004’s EuroTrip, as he belts out a punk-rock song about cuckolding poor Scotty.
body: Damon, Cooper, and Murray are no strangers to comedy; so it comes as no surprise that they’d delight in taking these small roles for the sake of a good bit. But the most iconic surprise celebrity cameo of all time came in 2008, thanks largely to the fact that a satirical comedy put an always-serious A-list action star in a bald cap and fat suit, with layers and layers of body hair that extended all the way to his knuckles.

In Tropic Thunder, Tom Cruise plays Les Grossman, a despicable film studio executive who is so outrageous you almost can’t even believe it’s him. It remains perhaps the single wildest performance of Cruise’s career, and you can now watch all of Tropic Thunder for free with ads on YouTube.

articles.title: Silent Hill Producer Says Konami Wants to Release a New Game in the Series Every Year
articles.summary: Silent Hill producer Motoi Okamoto says that Konami is gunning for annual releases of new games in its flagship horror franchise. Okamoto divulged this news in an interview with Gamesradar at Gamescom 2026, explaining that Konami is looking for fresh takes on the well-trodden beats of the Silent…
body: "Our aim is to, hopefully, have an annual release of new games," he told the outlet. “If we stay laser-focused on the same American setting, that would exhaust [narrative] possibilities, and also potentially cause fatigue for the playerbase."

Okamoto also confirmed that several unannounced Silent Hill projects are currently in development. "There are still many projects that are still [in] the works and very unannounced titles. So obviously, we can't go into specifics. But there are still many projects that we are currently exploring and working on as we speak,” he said.

"We would like to let players know that we have more experiences coming up, and many types of games that, we believe, will be able to provide positive kinds of surprises for players waiting for this for the series."

articles.title: Portal-Like Shooter Splitgate Died Once, And It’s Dying Again … Kind Of
articles.summary: Some games just aren't long for this world, and that’s exactly the case with the Portal-like and Halo-like shooter Splitgate: Arena Reloaded, which is getting put on a form of life support starting in early September. Developer 1047 Games took to X on August 26 to announce the news.
body: "The reality is that neither game is generating enough revenue to support the ongoing cost of dedicated servers," 1047 Games said. "We have continued covering the costs because we wanted to give both games every opportunity to grow, but we have reached the point where that is no longer sustainable. We have loved working on these games, playing them, and building them with this community, and we wish we could continue supporting them."

Despite development ending for both games, 1047 Games said that neither one will simply get shut down. Instead, both Empulse and Splitgate: Arena Reloaded have been "reworked to support peer-to-peer play." So, starting September 3, the dedicated servers will go offline, and both games will be playable for the foreseeable future through a P2P server-hosting browser. This means that you'll only be able to find matches when other people are online and hosting games instead of relying on servers to find games for you.

This is exactly what happened with the first Splitgate in August 2025. Released in 2019, the dedicated servers went offline on August 29, 2025, and entered a similar peer-to-peer multiplayer environment.

articles.title: All The Goth Girlies Who Loved American McGee’s Alice Need To See This Game
articles.summary: Now that Gamescom has kicked off, a seemingly endless barrage of new game trailers are hitting social media, and it's easy for smaller projects to get lost in the shuffle.
body: In Cutout, players control Lena, a "child of the forest" who takes the form of a 2D paper doll. After discovering a pair of scissors--and tapping into her internal rage--Lena embarks on a quest through a grimdark fairytale world full of enemies whose limbs she can sever and attach to her own body, giving her unique powers. But there's a catch: Enemies can also steal Lena's limbs and use them against her in battle.
In addition to stealing various limbs for advantage in combat, players will also be faced with choices that will shape what kind of person Lena becomes.
"Will you claim what they denied you, or heal what they destroyed?" an unseen narrator asks in the game's trailer.

From the spooky-cute fairytale aesthetic to the surprisingly violent premise and even Lena's striped stockings, Cutout is definitely giving off major Alice vibes (with a dash of Little Nightmares in there, too). We'll likely never get another Alice game from American McGee (thanks, EA), but with Cutout on the way, fans of nightmarish fairytales finally have a spiritual successor to look forward to.

articles.title: Michael B. Jordan’s Near-Perfect Action Trilogy Is About to Leave Netflix
articles.summary: Rocky V was a huge mistake. After four successful, crowd-pleasing movies about Italian-American boxer Rocky Balboa, Sylvester Stallone pressed his luck with a fifth one released in 1990 that everyone hated, mostly thanks to the fact that it was about Rocky training a punk kid nobody liked.
body: That bothered Stallone. Rocky was his breakthrough character. He had written the screenplay in the 1970s and held out on a deal until a studio agreed for him to play the lead. The film became a hit and went on to win Best Picture at the Oscars. Rocky meant a lot to Stallone and he hated that his signature character might end on such a down-note. So he wrote, directed, and starred in 2006's Rocky Balboa, which saw an aged Rocky prove he’s still got it in one last fight. The movie perfectly hit the mark for fans of the franchise and was clearly meant to be the end of the story.

Few people expected to see Rocky again, especially not as a trainer like in Rocky V, but that’s precisely the position he filled when he returned to the big screen for a whole new franchise which eventually became the Creed trilogy. All three of those films are excellent, and they're all leaving Netflix on August 31, so it’s worth catching them before the bell rings.

articles.title: GTA 6 Wants You To Reconsider Doing What Everyone Does In Grand Theft Auto
articles.summary: A new deep dive has dropped with some fascinating takeaways from Rockstar Games on the most anticipated release of the year, Grand Theft Auto 6. We've learned a lot already, including a feature returning from San Andreas and how switching between the two protagonists works.
body: In the Autumn 2026 Issue of Dazed magazine, some Rockstar Games developers talked about what you can expect when GTA 6 drops this November. While you're probably looking forward to rampaging through Leonida as you'd do in just about every other GTA game, the team is really cautioning you from doing so.

Because GTA 6 puts a greater emphasis on visual feedback (especially regarding how activities like exercising impact protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos appearance) and the deeper relationships you can have between the two main characters and all the other characters, GTA 6 features a heightened realism that makes you think twice about what you do and how you do it.

articles.title: David Fincher and Quentin Tarantino's Once Upon a Time in Hollywood Sequel Gets Official Release Update
articles.summary: Quentin Tarantino's Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood is getting an official sequel, one not directed by Tarantino himself. Seven and Fight Club director David Fincher is helming it instead with a new story that focuses on Brad Pitt's stuntman character Cliff Booth.
body: The Adventures of Cliff Booth has been retitled The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth — for reasons unknown — and will make its Netflix debut on Dec. 23.

Fincher and Tarantino fans will get an early look at the film in November. Netflix reconfirmed an exclusive two-week run in IMAX theaters globally starting Nov. 25. So if you want to see what a Fincher-led sequel to Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood looks like on the biggest screen, you have a limited window.

Pitt will reprise his Best Supporting Actor Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth in the film. While the original film was set in 1969, the sequel will take place in 1977 in "a very different Hollywood," Netflix says. The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Peter Weller, Matt Groove, JB Tadena, Corey Fogelmanis, and Karren Karagulian. Fincher directed from a script written by Tarantino, the latter of which has not revealed his 10th and final film-directing project.

articles.title: Lego Unveils Massive New Star Wars 6,130-Piece Set Inspired by the Empire Strikes Back
articles.summary: When it comes to Star Wars, Lego likes to go big. Three of Lego's biggest sets are Star Wars sets: The Lego Death Star, released in 2025, reigns supreme in sheer size with its 9,023-piece recreation of the Empire's super weapon.
body: With its 6,130-piece build, the Lego Star Wars Executor Super Star Destroyer set won't dethrone the other gargantuan Lego Star Wars sets, but it does set one new record. It's now "the longest Lego Star Wars brick-built model to date," the toy maker said.

The Lego Star Wars Executor Super Star Destroyer is based on the comically long flagship used by Darth Vader in Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back. The Lego version of Vader's Star Destroyer — which measures 19,000 meters long in Star Wars canon, Wookieepedia tells us — is an impressive 53.5 inches (136 cm) in length. To achieve this impressive feat, Lego says, the set's design team "engineered a Lego System core with slender Lego Technic outriggers that anchor the exterior panels, delivering strength without bulk."

articles.title: Brütal Legend is available free in honor of Tim Curry
articles.summary: Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames,
body: Tim Curry has died at the age of 80, leaving behind a rich legacy in movies, television, and videogames. As well as playing Gabriel Knight, Premier Anatoly Cherdenko in Red Alert 3, and Arl Howe in Dragon Age: Origins, Curry voiced the villainous Doviculus in Double Fine's heavy metal epic Brütal Legend. To pay tribute to his passing, Brütal Legend is currently available for free on itch for a very metal 666 minutes. You can download it now, or claim it to download later.

This isn't the first time Double Fine has given their game away for free. Last time it was in honor of Ozzy Osbourne, who has a cameo as the Guardian of Metal shopkeeper in Brütal Legend, and likewise it was made available for 666 minutes. At the time of writing, that means you have a little over nine hours to claim it.

articles.summary: We've had you identify games just based on a screenshot of their open world, but could you do the same if I made the quiz a little more specific? Maybe test your water hazard knowledge? More quizzes! Want to keep testing your knowledge of gaming trivia?
body: Well, I plan to do just that, so turn back now if big bodies of open water activate your fight-or-flight. I won't judge you (they do the same thing to me), but I delight in terrifying myself into clenching every muscle in my body. Remember the Sea Hag from Tomb Raider Chronicles? She must've given me my first tension headache.

Anyway, the lakes, oceans, and various water levels in games aren't always scary. In fact, most games on this list aren't, and I've sampled a bit of everything to include water in all its shapes. Some answers are here just because they're serene eye candy, while others are memorably nasty. They may not share a common theme either, so be ready to recall games with water exploration as a focus, and games that hardly let you dip a toe in.

Now that you've been briefed, will you sink or swim? You've got 10 minutes to identify 15 games by a screenshot of their water. When you're done, let us know how you did! I'll be over here rooting for you from a safe distance in the shallow end.

articles.title: Dark Souls meets Weird West in Guns of Eschaton, and it's a refreshing FPS shake-up for the well-worn formula - even if it's a bit bloody hard
articles.summary: Look, I'll level with you: I was rubbish at Guns of Eschaton during my recent hands-on time. There are some very obvious reasons for that - it's a hard game that doesn't currently especially explain itself very well, for one.
body: And with the tutorial out the way, Guns of Eschaton shows even less mercy. Once you reach its first proper area (the game's action is split across multiple discrete locations, accessed via a spooky hub known as Hounds Camp), you've suddenly got to contend with multiple enemies attacking from all directions, some enemies charging in from around corners and others, unsportingly, sniping from afar. Most areas, including the Spaghetti Western sprawl of pueblos blanco that open the game, require you to locate and defeat a boss. And death is almost an inevitability until you attune yourself to Guns of Eschaton's ways.

And there's more! Weapon modifications are supposedly possible at certain branches in the story, so you might choose to strip away the Buffalo Rifle's handy scope attachment in order to invoke the spirit inside, essentially turning it into a powerful one-shot revolver. Further tweaks come via ammo mods that add multiplier effects to the likes of range damage and recoil. And that's on top of armour, and consumables like dynamite and throwing knives.

videos.title: Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy - PS5/PS5 Pro/Series X/S Tech Review - Superb On All Systems
videos.summary: Thanks to MSI for sponsoring this video. Purchase an eligible QD-OLED display and share your feedback for the chance to get a game code for Onimusha: Way of the Sword
body: Developer Asobo Studio returns with its most sumptuous looking adventure yet. Here the PS5 Pro gets the spotlight with boosted resolutions, PSSR support and slicker frame-rates than base PS5. The ability to unlock all versions to 120fps (barring Series S) is also hugely useful, and the recommend pick if you have a VRR display - and if not, there are plenty of other modes to choose from. Tom covers each in detail.
points: Purchase an eligible QD-OLED display and share your feedback for the chance to get a game code for Onimusha: Way of the Sword
